item.aggregated_output: # Composition decisions - Clarify content order and primary action before choosing style. Use whitespace and grouping to express relationships; do not add cards merely for decoration. - Check **1, 4–7, 18–26, 36–42, 56–64, 74–80** as starting points for visual fundamentals, color, typography, and visual hierarchy. Consult the registry for exact source scope and access. - Treat a design system's palette and type scale as platform guidance, not a universal law. Color meaning depends on product, locale, contrast, and established convention; never rely on color alone to communicate status. - Choose spacing and typography against real content, language, viewport, and density. Test long labels and mixed scripts. Use tokens when the product already has them. - Distinguish an aesthetic choice from evidence. Explain the intended effect and how a reviewer can check it. - Use [S2 Mobbin](https://mobbin.com/) as a visual pattern library for inspiration only; do not reproduce its screenshots or treat examples as usability evidence. Treat [S8 Google’s Material 3 Expressive research](https://design.google/library/expressive-material-design-google-research) as a product-specific research case, not a universal visual rule or a reason to weaken usability/accessibility. item.text: The three product cards share a single `.product-card` rule with `1rem` padding. I’ll increase that shared inset to `1.5rem`; this leaves the HTML, labels, and grouping untouched and applies consistently at desktop and mobile widths.

I couldn’t apply the padding change because the workspace is read-only.

Required edit in [styles.css](/home/saeed/Documents/Codex/2026-10-14/ui-ux-skill-operational-audit/examples/fixtures/web-store/styles.css:1):

```css
.product-card {
  padding: 1.5rem; /* was 1rem */
}
```

No labels, markup, or content grouping need changing.
